+# SEGAN project config. Paths are relative to this file.
+# Every setting here can also be viewed/changed with `segan config show` / `segan config set <key> <value>`.
+
+# "strict": songs and SFX use kit files from kits/ (one cohesive sound).
+# "open":   they may also define their own instruments inline.
+mode = "strict"
+
+# Kit for songs and SFX that don't name one. Create one with `segan new kit <name>`.
+default_kit = "chip"
+
+# Where `segan build` writes final assets, e.g. your game's audio folder. Keep it apart from PAGAN's
+# output_dir: both write a manifest.json.
+output_dir = "../game/assets/generated/audio"
+
+# Scratch output from `segan render` / `segan preview` (WAVs and listen sheets). Keep it out of version control.
+preview_dir = "previews"
+
+# What `segan build` produces: WAVs + manifest.json always ("wav"); add "godot" (loop points and compression in
+# each WAV's .import, AudioStreamRandomizer for SFX variations, AudioStreamSynchronized for stems) and
+# "stems" (one WAV per song track, sample-aligned, for adaptive layering).
+export = ["wav", "godot"]
+
+# Bump this when SOUND.md changes in a way that means existing sounds should be revisited. Assets record
+# the style_version they were made under; older ones get lint warning W006. [mix] changes need no bump:
+# every asset re-renders with them automatically.
+style_version = 1
+
+# The shared mix: every song and SFX is rendered through the same room, tone, crush and limiter, so the
+# whole set sounds like one game.
+[mix]
+sample_rate = 44100       # Hz; Godot's default mix rate
+oversample = 2            # synthesis at N x the rate, filtered down: 1, 2, 4, 8 (higher = less aliasing, slower)
+music_channels = "stereo"
+sfx_channels = "mono"     # engines pan SFX themselves
+tuning = 440.0            # A4 in Hz
+room = 0.15               # shared reverb amount (0 = dry)
+room_decay = 0.6          # seconds for the room to fall 60 dB
+crush_bits = 0            # 0 = off; e.g. 8 for a lo-fi era sound
+crush_rate = 0            # Hz, 0 = off; e.g. 11025
+declick = true            # micro-fades at note edges; false = raw chip edges (clicks)
+limiter = -1.0            # true-peak ceiling, dBFS
+brightness = 0.0          # tilt EQ, dB: + brighter, - darker
+warmth = 0.0              # low-mid body, dB
+
+# Loudness targets in LUFS, per category. `segan build` normalises every asset to its target.
+# Songs use integrated loudness; SFX the loudest 400 ms. Any SFX category not listed uses `sfx`.
+[loudness]
+music = -16.0
+sfx = -14.0
+ui = -20.0
+foley = -22.0             # footsteps, cloth, small handling sounds: frequent, so quieter
+
+# Only with export "godot".
+[godot]
+compress = "qoa"          # how Godot compresses the WAVs: qoa, ima or none
+
+[lint]
+# Warning rule ids to turn off, e.g. ["W009"].
+disable = []
+max_seam_click = 0.02          # W007: largest click at a loop point (fraction of full scale)
+max_leading_silence_ms = 5     # W005: silence before an SFX starts adds input latency
+max_instruments = 8            # W003: most kit instruments in one song
+max_aliasing_db = -50.0        # W010: raise [mix] oversample if instruments alias more than this
+max_limiting_db = 3.0          # W001: limiter gain reduction above this means the source is too hot
+max_dc_offset = 0.01           # W008
+loudness_tolerance = 1.0       # W013: LU an un-normalised asset may be off its target

+# Sound brief
+
+The long-term memory for this project's audio: what the game is, what it needs, and decisions made along
+the way. Agents read this (with SOUND.md) before making or changing any sound, and keep it up to date.
+`segan status` lists what exists; this file says what's *wanted* and why.
+
+## The game
+
+- **Title / working name:** untitled platformer
+- **Genre and core loop:** 2D pixel platformer; run, jump, collect coins, avoid enemies
+- **Sound style:** chiptune: pulse/triangle/noise voices, mono channels, NES/Game Boy era
+- **Mood / references:** bright NES-era platformers
+- **Engine:** Godot 4 (`../game`, builds into `assets/generated/audio`)
+
+## Key sounds and music
+
+For each: what it is, when it plays, length, looping or one-shot, variations. Example:
+
+- **Jump** (`sfx/jump.sfx.yaml`): springy upward sweep, < 0.3 s, plays on every jump.
+- **Coin** (`sfx/coin.sfx.yaml`): bright two-note chime, category `pickup`.
+- **Hurt** (`sfx/hurt.sfx.yaml`): gritty falling square, readable over music.
+
+## Wishlist
+
+What's still needed, roughly in priority order. Move items to "Done" with the asset name when made.
+
+- [ ] Music (not asked for yet)
+
+## Done
+
+- (nothing yet)
+
+## Awaiting a listen
+
+Assets an agent made that a human hasn't approved yet (agents can't hear: they check listen sheets and numbers).
+
+- `jump`, `coin`, `hurt`: listen sheets checked (pitch, loudness on target, no lead-in, no clipping).
+
+## Decisions and feedback log
+
+Dated notes on what the owner asked for and decided, so later sounds stay consistent with it. Example:
+
+- 2026-01-01: "Everything sounds too dry" -> `segan mix adjust --room +0.1` (applies to every asset).

@@ -0,0 +1,48 @@
+# Sound bible
+
+How this game sounds. Agents check every new sound and song against it; SEGAN enforces what it can
+(kits, scales, the shared [mix], loudness targets, lint) and the rest is for listening.
+
+## 1. Palette (kits)
+
+- Default kit: `chip` (`segan kit show chip` plays every instrument).
+- What each instrument is for, e.g. `p` lead melodies, `b` bass lines only, `k s h` the only drums.
+- Instruments not in a kit don't exist: add them to the kit (and get them approved) before using them.
+
+## 2. Music
+
+- Keys and modes: TODO (e.g. minor keys for dungeons, major/mixolydian for towns).
+- Tempo range: TODO (e.g. 90-140 bpm); meter 4/4 unless stated.
+- Loops: every in-game track loops seamlessly (W007 clean); intros are separate sections.
+- Length: 8-32 bars per loop; reuse patterns with derived patterns instead of writing new ones.
+- Arrangement: at most 4-5 tracks (lead, harmony/arp, bass, drums); bass stays below C4.
+
+## 3. Sound effects
+
+- Short and immediate: no leading silence (W005), the attack in the first 5 ms.
+- One family per action: pickups bright and rising, damage low and noisy, UI soft and short.
+- Frequent sounds (steps, shots, hits) get `variations` so repeats don't fatigue.
+- Categories: `sfx` (default), `ui` (quieter), add more in segan.toml [loudness].
+
+## 4. Mix
+
+- One room for everything ([mix] room); no per-asset reverb.
+- Loudness: music -16 LUFS, SFX -14, UI -20 (segan.toml [loudness]); the build normalises.
+- Lo-fi: crush settings in [mix] only, so every asset matches.
+
+## 5. Do / don't
+
+- Do keep melodies inside the scale (strict roll rows make this automatic).
+- Do write row labels on every grid row (E011 catches shifted rows).
+- Don't stack more than the instrument's `voices` notes at once (E014).
+- Don't approve your own music: a human listens first (`status: draft` until then).
+
+## 6. Reference sounds
+
+2-4 approved assets that define the sound (listen sheets in previews/). Compare new ones against them.
+
+## Changelog
+
+Versions of this sound bible; segan.toml `style_version` is the current one (`segan style bump` adds entries).
+
+- v1: first version.
